ad2.lead: The Smart Truck (AD2 kit) is a ₹2,50,000 forward-camera, radar, compute-box, driver-display and harness assembly for N2/N3 commercial vehicles, sold into a compliance-driven market created by the ADAS mandate. It is the single largest SKU in the DeepGrid portfolio, representing 39.9% of projected FY2032 group revenue at 89% gross margin, a concentration that makes its certification and installation milestones the primary risk to the entire plan.

useCases.title: Regulatory retrofit for existing trucks
useCases.buyer: Fleet operators and retrofit installers
useCases.problem: Fleet operators must fit ADAS systems to existing N2/N3 trucks to comply with the ADAS mandate covering driver-drowsiness, blind-spot and lane-departure obligations; the decision is compliance-led, not discretionary.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies the complete AD2 kit, camera, 4D radar, SoC2 compute box, driver display and vehicle-bus harness, through fleet-direct and retrofit-installer channels, enabling fitment without OEM involvement.

useCases.title: OEM line-fit on new trucks
useCases.buyer: Truck OEMs and OEM homologation engineers
useCases.problem: Truck OEMs must offer AIS-162/188-certified ADAS on new N2/N3 models to meet the mandate, requiring a certified, integrable kit that can be validated through ARAI or ICAT.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies the same AD2 architecture certified to AIS-162/188, sold to OEM or Tier-1 at the listed price, with the compute module designed for an ASIC swap-in as owned 28 nm silicon becomes available.

useCases.title: Driver drowsiness compliance study
useCases.buyer: Fleet safety managers and OEM homologation engineers
useCases.problem: AIS-184 (DDAWS) requires manufacturers to run a ten-participant day-and-night study generating ten or more true-positive or false-negative events and to deliver per-participant sensitivity data before approval, a documentation burden most integrators cannot self-assemble.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies an in-cab infrared drowsiness pipeline, eyelid closure, gaze, head pose and PERCLOS-class metrics fused with vehicle signals, together with the completed ten-participant study, thresholds, activation speed, weather limits and the full statistical documentation package.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The kit follows a four-stage signal chain: camera and radar monitor the forward path and blind quarters; the SoC2 compute box fuses both into a single object list carrying range and closing speed; collision, lane-departure and blind-spot logic determine whether a warning is needed; and the driver is alerted, with the brake interface signalled where the vehicle supports it. The compute box accepts eleven configured inputs simultaneously, seven 8MP RGB cameras on GMSL2, two thermal cameras and front/rear 4D 77 GHz radar, and completes fusion in a claimed 8.6 ms of a 33.3 ms frame budget. Management states this leaves 74% of the frame budget unused, which is the margin that allows one part to serve every sensor configuration below it; however, an internal review notes that the 8.6 ms figure requires validation of which acquisition, inference and fusion stages it includes, and that the remainder is budget arithmetic rather than independently demonstrated system headroom. Closing speed derived from radar is the variable that a braking decision actually turns on, which is why radar is treated as a required input rather than an optional one.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The ADAS mandate creates a non-discretionary demand pool: MoRTH figures cited in the deck show 0.5 million new N2/N3 trucks per year plus 0.5 million retrofit candidates, and the mandate covers driver-drowsiness, blind-spot and lane-departure obligations on those vehicle classes. AIS-184 (DDAWS) obligations apply from 1 October 2027 for new models and 1 January 2028 for all models, setting a hard compliance calendar that fleet operators and OEMs cannot defer. DeepGrid's FY2032 volume target of 18,000 units represents a management-assumed capture rate of 1.80% of that pool, meaning the product does not require market creation, it requires certification and installation capacity to be in place before the compliance dates. The ramp from 3 units in FY2027 to 18,000 in FY2032 is gated by ARAI or ICAT certification and by building installer throughput to match volume, not by demand generation.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The kit is sold as a product at ₹2,50,000 per unit with an 89% gross margin, the same margin carried across the road-autonomy surface; the high margin reflects that the reusable asset is the SoC2 silicon and software, with the sensor installation treated as one application of that platform. Revenue is projected to ramp from ₹2 Cr in FY2028 to ₹35 Cr in FY2029, ₹100 Cr in FY2030, ₹225 Cr in FY2031 and ₹450 Cr in FY2032, all figures are management projections. The planned ASIC swap-in, replacing an FPGA compute module with owned 28 nm silicon at the same price, is the mechanism for the margin to hold or improve as volume scales, because the unit price is held flat while silicon cost falls. A software-attach layer, T100 AI licensing, fleet data-as-a-service and DMS-compliance reporting, is described as a subsequent revenue phase, though it is characterised internally as optionality rather than base case.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Three things must land in sequence: certification through ARAI or ICAT, installation capacity at 18,000 fitments per year, and fleet access. Certification is the first gate because no revenue is possible without it, and the 8.6 ms processing claim and radar verification milestones are open items that must be closed as part of that process. Installation capacity is a physical constraint, 18,000 fitments per year requires a trained installer network that does not yet exist at that scale, and the ramp schedule leaves no slack if channel build lags. The concentration risk is acute: Smart Truck (AD2 kit) and the AD0 Smart Mirror are the same product family sold to overlapping buyers, so a single certification or installation delay hits ₹720 Cr of projected FY2032 revenue simultaneously, which is larger than the other thirteen SKUs combined.

facts.text: FY2032 revenue projection: ₹450 Cr at 18,000 units and 89% gross margin, representing 39.9% of projected group revenue. Management projection.

Demand pool: 0.5 million new N2/N3 trucks per year plus 0.5 million retrofit candidates; FY2032 volume of 18,000 units equals a 1.80% capture rate. Pool sizes are third-party published estimates; capture rate is a management assumption.

Processing claim: 8.6 ms of a 33.3 ms frame budget for eleven-input fused perception, leaving an arithmetic remainder of 24.7 ms (74% of the frame). An internal review notes this is budget arithmetic, not independently demonstrated system headroom.

Concentration exposure: Smart Truck (AD2 kit) at ₹450 Cr and AD0 Smart Mirror at ₹270 Cr together represent ₹720 Cr, larger than the other thirteen SKUs combined; a shared certification or installation delay hits both simultaneously. Management projection.

taas.lead: Autonomous TaaS is a contracted autonomous-trucking service in which DeepGrid owns the vehicle, runs the full SoC2 autonomy stack, and bills logistics operators per trip or per tonne rather than selling hardware. It is the highest-revenue-per-unit line in the portfolio at ₹66 lakh per vehicle, and the only line where DeepGrid captures operating margin instead of a hardware margin.

useCases.title: Fixed-route logistics operations
useCases.buyer: Logistics operators on fixed, repeatable routes where an autonomous lane can be proven
useCases.problem: Operators must move freight at competitive cost per tonne-kilometre on defined corridors, and on many routes the binding constraint is finding a qualified driver at all, not merely driver cost.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies the vehicle with the full AD2 sensor set, the SoC2 autonomy stack, remote operations and monitoring, and route commissioning as a single metered service contract, billed per trip or per tonne.

useCases.title: Autonomous container-yard movement (Seaport AGV)
useCases.buyer: Port and terminal operators automating container movement
useCases.problem: Terminal operators must move containers between quay cranes and yard blocks continuously, in tight lanes with heavy overhead equipment, while controlling labour cost inside a controlled, geofenced site.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies an autonomous container-yard vehicle with surround sensing, SoC2 compute and autonomy stack, and yard-management system integration, holding 7 cm positioning in the open and 22 cm under the crane where RTK-GNSS alone degrades.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The vehicle's full sensor set reads a route that DeepGrid has already surveyed and mapped. The SoC2 then runs the autonomy stack against that stored route model, the same perception-compute silicon used across every SKU in the portfolio, operating under different firmware. Fleet logic schedules dispatch, sequences routes, and hands off to a remote operator when the situation exceeds what the vehicle should decide autonomously. The customer is billed per trip or per tonne; no hardware changes hands.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Driver availability on fixed freight corridors is becoming a binding operational constraint, not merely a cost line, making autonomous substitution commercially attractive independent of wage arbitrage. The India trucking fleet runs at 0.6–0.8 million units per year, and DeepGrid's FY2032 target of 100 vehicles represents 0.01% capture of that pool, a threshold management characterises as reachable through direct, one-route-at-a-time commercial contracts. The TaaS model also benefits from the same SoC2 silicon development already funded for the broader ADAS portfolio, so the marginal cost of extending the stack to an owned-and-operated vehicle is low. First revenue is projected for FY2028, giving three years of route-level proof before the plan reaches scale.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: Because DeepGrid owns the asset and bills for the service rather than selling hardware, it captures the operating margin on every kilometre driven rather than a one-time product margin. The projected gross margin is 89% at FY2032 on ₹66 Cr of revenue across 100 vehicles, these are management projections. Fleet capital expenditure of approximately ₹60 Cr (cumulative) is structured as asset-backed debt or lease finance against the trucks themselves, explicitly kept off the equity cash, so the equity round funds silicon development rather than vehicle procurement. Interest on that fleet debt is modelled at 15% per annum, reaching ₹9 Cr annually by FY2032.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Regulatory clearance for autonomous operation in controlled corridors is the primary external dependency; without route-level permission, no vehicle can operate commercially. Asset finance must be secured against the trucks rather than drawn from equity, and lenders must accept an autonomous-vehicle asset as collateral, a condition that has not yet been tested at scale in India. Each commercial contract is won one route at a time through direct negotiation, so revenue ramp depends on the pace of route commissioning and operator willingness to commit to a novel service model. The product also carries operational risk that the hardware product lines do not: DeepGrid owns the asset and is responsible for uptime, making fleet reliability a direct P&L exposure.

facts.text: Listed price: ₹66.00 L per vehicle, the highest revenue per unit in the DeepGrid portfolio.
FY2032 revenue projection: ₹66 Cr at 89% gross margin across 100 units, equal to 5.8% of group plan revenue, management projection.
Fleet capex: approximately ₹60 Cr cumulative by FY2032, structured as debt or lease finance against the trucks at a modelled interest rate of 15% per annum, not drawn from the equity raise.

Demand pool: India trucking 0.6–0.8 million units per year; FY2032 target of 100 vehicles represents 0.01% capture, capture rate is a management assumption, pool size is a third-party published estimate.

ad0.lead: The AD0 Smart Mirror is a replacement rear-view mirror with an integrated display, four body cameras and a wiring loom that fits in an afternoon and ships first among DeepGrid's fifteen products. No mandate drives its purchase, buyers pay voluntarily for visibility and parking safety, yet it is projected to contribute ₹270 Cr at 89% gross margin by FY2032, making it the second-largest revenue line in the portfolio.

useCases.title: Personal vehicle and small-fleet safety upgrade
useCases.buyer: Vehicle owners and small fleets
useCases.problem: Drivers of personal vehicles and small fleets lack visibility into blind quarters during parking and low-speed manoeuvres, creating collision risk they choose to address as an accessory purchase rather than a mandated requirement.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies a drop-in mirror unit containing four surround cameras, a mirror-format display, SoC2 compute and an alert speaker; the system stitches a 360° view and issues directional alerts when anything enters the danger zone.

useCases.title: Aftermarket retail and fitment-shop channel
useCases.buyer: Aftermarket accessory retail and fitment shops, plus OEM accessory catalogues
useCases.problem: Fitment shops and accessory retailers need a competitively priced, easy-to-install surround-view product they can sell and fit without specialist tooling or vehicle-programme integration.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies a self-contained unit at ₹50,000 with a wiring loom designed for afternoon installation, enabling the channel to offer a complete surround-view solution without calibration or homologation obligations.

useCases.title: Portfolio channel-building anchor
useCases.buyer: Vehicle owners and small fleets
useCases.problem: DeepGrid's harder, higher-value road-autonomy products require an established distribution and fitment network before they can scale; that network does not exist at launch.
useCases.delivers: AD0, as the highest-unit-count SKU with the lowest fitment complexity, builds the aftermarket channel and customer relationships that the AD1 and AD2 products inherit as they reach market.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Four body cameras cover the vehicle's blind quarters and feed raw video into the SoC2 compute integrated in the mirror head unit. The SoC2 stitches the four feeds into a single 360° surround image and runs proximity and motion logic to flag anything entering the danger zone. The driver sees the stitched view on the mirror-format display and hears a directional alert. The same SoC2 perception stage is common to every DeepGrid SKU; for AD0 it runs under firmware appropriate to this passive-alert role, and the product operates on current-generation hardware without waiting for the next-generation ASIC.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: No regulatory mandate applies to the AD0 Smart Mirror; the Demand & TAM sheet explicitly classifies it as a voluntary safety and convenience buy, while the Revenue Build sheet labels it 'mandate retrofit', these two internal documents disagree, and the distinction matters because mandate-driven and voluntary demand carry different risk profiles and sales cycles. What is clear is that the 360° surround-view market is already active, sized at $3.09B in 2025 with a 10.7% CAGR per Towards Automotive, so DeepGrid is entering an established category rather than creating one. The product runs on current-generation hardware and is not gated on the ASIC, allowing first revenue in FY2027 ahead of the nine SKUs that require production silicon. The FY2032 volume of 54,000 units represents a management-assumed capture of 0.93% of that existing market pool.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The unit price is ₹50,000, held flat across the six-year plan, so all revenue growth comes from volume rather than price appreciation. At that price and volume, management projects ₹270 Cr in FY2032 revenue at an 89% gross margin, making AD0 the second-largest contributor at 23.9% of group revenue. The ramp is gradual, 10 units in FY2027, 2,200 in FY2028, reaching 54,000 by FY2032, reflecting the time required to build distribution reach through aftermarket retail, fitment shops and OEM accessory catalogues. AD0 and the Smart Truck kit together account for 64% of FY2032 group revenue, so a distribution or pricing setback in this product family would affect ₹720 Cr at once, more than the other thirteen SKUs combined.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The two stated dependencies are distribution reach and price holding at ₹50,000; if either slips, the volume ramp and the margin both compress simultaneously. The internal disagreement between 'mandate retrofit' and 'NOT mandated, voluntary safety/convenience buy' is unresolved: if demand is purely voluntary, the sales cycle is longer and less predictable than a compliance-driven purchase, and the 54,000-unit FY2032 projection rests on a management-assumed 0.93% capture of an existing market rather than a regulatory floor. Because AD0 and the Smart Truck kit are sold to overlapping buyers through overlapping channels, any installation bottleneck or channel failure hits both lines together. Finally, AD0's role as the channel-builder for harder products means that underperformance here delays the distribution infrastructure that AD1 and AD2 depend on.

FY2032 management projection: 54,000 units, ₹270 Cr revenue, 89% gross margin, 23.9% of group revenue.
Market pool: existing 360° surround-view market sized at $3.09B in 2025 at 10.7% CAGR (Towards Automotive); FY2032 volume of 54,000 units is a management-assumed 0.93% capture of that pool.
Concentration risk: AD0 and Smart Truck together represent ₹720 Cr of FY2032 projected revenue, 64% of the group total and more than the other thirteen SKUs combined.

t100.lead: The T100 AI Licence is a subscription to DeepGrid's trained Indian-road perception models and toolchain, sold to third-party compute platforms that want to ship autonomous products without building their own dataset. At 94% gross margin with no bill of materials, it is the highest-margin line in the portfolio, but carries no sized demand pool and is treated by management as optionality rather than base case.

useCases.title: OEM platform integration
useCases.buyer: OEMs and platform partners
useCases.problem: OEMs building autonomous or ADAS products for Indian roads need perception models tuned to local traffic mix, lane discipline and lighting conditions, but collecting and training on Indian road data requires years of in-market operation they have not yet done.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid licences its trained India-road perception models, toolchain and deployment runtime so the OEM can integrate the perception layer into their own hardware and ship under their own brand, with continuous model updates delivered via the subscription.

useCases.title: Autonomous freight platform licensing
useCases.buyer: Autonomous freight platform operators
useCases.problem: Operators building autonomous freight systems need a perception stack validated on Indian roads to underpin their autonomy software, but lack the dataset and training infrastructure to develop one independently.
useCases.delivers: The T100 licence provides the perception SDK and update stream that runs inside the operator's runtime, enabling them to deploy an India-ready autonomy stack without owning the underlying data collection or model-training capability.

useCases.title: Industrial and warehouse autonomy platforms
useCases.buyer: Industrial platform partners
useCases.problem: Warehouse and port AGV platform builders need edge-AI perception capable of operating in unstructured Indian environments, and sourcing a foreign chip-tied model stack creates both cost and localisation barriers.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid's toolchain and runtime-agnostic model licence lets industrial platform partners run Indian-trained perception on their own hardware, with no board or bill of materials supplied by DeepGrid.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The customer supplies their own hardware and sensors; DeepGrid's trained perception models run inference inside the customer's runtime. The customer's system then makes decisions and acts, and ships the finished product under its own brand with DeepGrid's perception layer embedded. Because no board or component is manufactured or shipped, there is no bill of materials, it is the only line in the plan with that characteristic. Model updates are delivered continuously via the licence subscription, meaning the perception stack improves over the product's life without requiring a hardware change.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: First revenue is planned for FY2029, later than every other line in the portfolio, because a perception licence requires a demonstrated track record before any OEM will sign one. The delay is structural: the models must accumulate kilometres on Indian roads through DeepGrid's own hardware deployments before they carry enough credibility to be licensed independently. Foreign ADAS chips were designed for European and US roads and cannot be software-patched to understand Indian driving conditions; that requires retraining on Indian data, which requires being in the Indian market first. Management characterises this first-mover data position as compounding with every kilometre driven, widening the performance gap over time.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Two conditions must hold simultaneously: DeepGrid must establish a defensible model advantage, and it must secure a signed licence, neither is evidenced yet. The model advantage depends on the Indian road perception stack reaching sufficient maturity, which the plan dates to FY2029. A further risk is that licensing the core could undercut the systems business that accounts for approximately 88% of revenue, so the sequencing, hardware deployments first, licensing second, is load-bearing. If the hardware track record does not materialise on schedule, the licence line has no foundation on which to sell.

facts.text: Gross margin: 94%, enabled by zero bill of materials, no silicon, no board, no assembly is shipped with the licence.
FY2032 revenue (management projection): ₹50 Cr from 50 licences at ₹100 L each, representing 4.4% of projected group revenue.
Demand pool: none separately sized; the portfolio deck and investment memorandum both classify this revenue line as optionality rather than base case.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The product is the SoC2 die itself, TSMC 28 nm, roughly 57 mm², supplied tested and binned in tray or reel with no enclosure, cables or fitting. The signal chain is entirely the customer's: their sensors feed their own board, the SoC2 die performs perception compute inside their design, their software acts on the result, and their finished product ships with DeepGrid silicon inside it. DeepGrid supplies the die, a reference design, integration documentation and toolchain access; the buyer carries all board-level integration and their own safety case. An architecture proposal under development gives each of eight processing cores a local DMA engine with a 16-entry descriptor table and three-level address generator, removing a shared-dispatch bottleneck; a 470 ms to 85 ms frame-time figure has been published but is described on the slide as a proposal awaiting testbench evidence, not a measured result.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The buyer trigger is the desire for Indian-designed silicon and domestic supply rather than an imported module, with procurement policy often as decisive as technical specification. The global ADAS chip pool was estimated at $2.29 billion in 2024 with a 20.6% CAGR (source: EMR 2024); DeepGrid's FY2032 volume of 30,000 units represents a 0.25% capture of that pool, which is a management assumption. The channel is direct design-in engagements described as long cycle and high commitment, meaning relationships started now determine whether first revenue lands in FY2028. Qualified volume silicon is expected in H1 2028, and OEM design-in runs 18 to 30 months, so the window for securing those engagements is already open.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The die sells at ₹18,000 per unit at a 94% gross margin, the highest in the portfolio, because DeepGrid ships silicon and a datasheet and the customer absorbs all integration, certification and installation cost. Revenue is projected at ₹54 Cr in FY2032 at 30,000 units, equal to 4.8% of group revenue; these are management projections. Because there is no fitment channel, warranty logistics or installation crew behind this line, every rupee arrives without those cost layers. The fifteen SKUs share one die, so the tapeout investment is spread across the portfolio rather than charged solely to this product.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Every unit of this line is downstream of the ASIC tapeout: if the tapeout does not land or the die does not qualify, this revenue does not exist. The 470 ms to 85 ms compute-latency improvement is a proposal awaiting testbench evidence, and the local-DMA architecture estimate of approximately 600 LUTs per engine, roughly 4,800 for eight engines before arbitration and software, has not been validated on measured silicon. The 0.25% pool-capture rate is a management assumption; the $2.29 billion pool size is a third-party published estimate, and actual capture depends on qualification outcomes and procurement decisions not yet made. Design-in engagements are described as long cycle and high commitment, so any delay to qualified silicon directly compresses the time available to close the partnerships that underpin the FY2028 first-revenue date.

ad1.lead: The AD1 Indoor L4 Kit is a self-driving retrofit, sensor head, compute box and drive-by-wire interface, fitted to forklifts and tugs a site already owns. Because no homologation applies inside a private site, it ships full Level-4 autonomy years before equivalent road products can legally operate, making it the portfolio's earliest proof point for the road autonomy roadmap.

useCases.title: Warehouse automation
useCases.buyer: Warehouse and industrial operators
useCases.problem: Operators must move goods repetitively through aisles using vehicles they already own, without the budget or lead time to replace fleets with purpose-built AMRs.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid retrofits existing forklifts with a sensor head, SoC2 compute box and drive-by-wire interface so the vehicle drives a geofenced route autonomously at up to 1.5 m/s, stopping within ±5 cm of an obstacle, without replacing the underlying asset.

useCases.title: Port and campus AGV retrofit
useCases.buyer: Warehouse and industrial operators; material-handling integrators
useCases.problem: Port and campus operators run tugs and internal transport vehicles on fixed, repetitive routes where manual driving is costly but public-road homologation is irrelevant.
useCases.delivers: The same AD1 kit, sold direct to site operators or through material-handling integrators, converts existing tugs to geofenced L4 operation on the same SoC2 silicon used across the road autonomy portfolio.

useCases.title: Road-autonomy silicon validation
useCases.buyer: DeepGrid Semi (internal portfolio role)
useCases.problem: Road-autonomy products cannot legally operate at L4 on public roads until homologation is complete, leaving the SoC2 silicon without a closed-loop field deployment to validate against.
useCases.delivers: The AD1 kit runs the full sense-localise-plan-act stack in closed-loop on real sites from FY2028, generating evidence that the same chip and software can execute L4 behaviour before any road mandate takes effect.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The kit follows four stages: cameras and a 24 m LiDAR at 5 Hz read the aisle, load and people, then fuse into a single bird's-eye occupancy view; the SoC2 compute box localises the vehicle against a site map held onboard; the planner selects a path and speed for the geofenced route; and the drive-by-wire interface issues steer, throttle and brake commands directly to the vehicle. The vehicle steers itself rather than alerting a driver, making this the only product in the portfolio where the silicon runs closed-loop rather than in an advisory role. A geofenced safety zone travels with the vehicle and caps speed at 1.5 m/s, with obstacle stops to ±5 cm. Site mapping and commissioning tooling is included in the kit, but throughput of that commissioning work, a services capacity constraint, is the primary operational dependency.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Inside a private site no homologation applies, so the deployment decision is commercial rather than regulatory, and L4 can ship years before it is legal on a public road. This asymmetry is the reason the AD1 kit is scheduled for first revenue in FY2028 while road-autonomy products face certification timelines tied to AIS-162 and related mandates. The warehouse and industrial autonomy segment sits within a third-party estimated $4.8 billion edge-AI market (Dataintelo/GMI, 2025), giving operators a large and growing pool of comparable deployments to benchmark against. The kit also runs on exactly the same SoC2 silicon as the road products, so every indoor deployment accumulates closed-loop operational evidence that supports the road roadmap at no additional silicon cost.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The single most cited dependency is site mapping and commissioning throughput: this is a services capacity constraint, not a product one, meaning revenue is gated by how many sites DeepGrid can survey, map and commission per quarter rather than by kit availability. Volume ramp from 20 units in FY2028 to 4,200 in FY2032 requires that services capacity to scale in parallel with hardware production. sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Up to four cameras connect directly to the card, giving full surround coverage; the SoC2 runs perception across all four streams in parallel and passes structured object lists and alerts to the host system over the PCIe interface. The memory architecture is central to why four channels is feasible on one card: each compute cube runs its own local DMA against an eight-bank L2 cache, which keeps utilisation high rather than starving on a single shared global DMA path. The host system, which provides the enclosure, thermal management and power, consumes the structured perception data and builds its own product on top, so DeepGrid supplies the compute and models while the customer retains control of their platform. The card ships with an SDK and model toolchain, reducing the integration burden for design-in customers.

sections.text: First revenue is planned for FY2028, the same year the ASIC era begins across the portfolio; FY2027 revenue across all SKUs is FPGA-based only, so the PCIe card's ramp is directly gated by SoC2 silicon availability. The addressable market for automotive edge-AI accelerator modules is cited by Dataintelo at $4.8B in 2025, growing to $22.6B by 2034 at a 21% CAGR, creating a window for a design-in before the market consolidates around established suppliers. Regulatory pressure under AIS-184, AIS-186 and AIS-187 is pulling OEMs toward validated multi-camera perception solutions on a fixed timetable, which shortens the sales cycle for a card that arrives with a working model stack. useCases.title: Forward reconnaissance and logistics
useCases.buyer: Indian Army and MoD procurement programmes
useCases.problem: The Army needs to conduct reconnaissance and logistics runs in terrain where sending personnel creates unacceptable risk; the buying cycle is measured in years and once a platform is qualified it is very hard to displace.

useCases.buyer: Indian Army and MoD procurement programmes
useCases.problem: Static perimeter security generates high false-alarm rates because individual sensor tracks, a vehicle on an access road, a person at a fence, are evaluated in isolation rather than correlated into a single threat picture.
useCases.delivers: The DGrid Sentinel perception stack fuses radar, thermal and camera tracks, escalates a combined threat along a timed loiter-to-breach-risk ladder, and hands the target off across ground sensors, patrol drone and sea buoy, while holding benign tracks without escalation to keep false-alarm rates low.

useCases.buyer: Indian Army and MoD procurement programmes

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The signal chain follows four stages common to every DeepGrid product: surround sensing reads terrain, obstacles and people; SoC2 builds a local map and plans a traversable route; the autonomy stack drives while a teleoperator can take control; and the mission payload executes its task at the destination. For defence use the fusion stack is pointed outward rather than forward, radar, thermal and camera tracks along a perimeter are classified individually and then correlated, so a vehicle loitering on an access road and a person approaching the fence stop being two unrelated contacts. Military-grade AES-256 encryption and lockstep RISC-V run on the secure enclave inside SoC2, and all data relay to the command post is encrypted. The DGrid Sentinel demonstrator, validated in a production-stack simulator, shows the decision layer correlating, escalating and handing off tracks, though this is simulation evidence, not a fielded deployment.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Indigenous-procurement rules structurally exclude import-dependent competitors from Indian defence tenders by specification, not by price, giving D-HUMR a near-zero-competition lane that does not depend on any automotive mandate. Revenue has already been received on this line on FPGA hardware, making it the portfolio's earliest external validation and demonstrating that the procurement channel is open. The MCEME pipeline and iDEX programmes provide a defined route to scale, and once a platform is qualified in defence procurement it is very hard to displace. The key constraint is not technical readiness but the slow, lumpy nature of defence procurement cycles and the requirement for security clearances.

The board runs perception across both streams on a single SoC2 die and returns a fused output to the customer's application, which then acts on it. Two channels is the first configuration where fusion becomes necessary, reconciling two views of the same scene into one object list, and it is the first configuration that justifies the hardware transformer path rather than a general-purpose processor. On the demand side, the 0.20% market-capture assumption must hold: the buyer is an integrator choosing between DeepGrid's module and competing edge-AI compute options in a market that incumbents already serve. Distribution through electronics channels adds a route to market but also introduces a dependency on channel partners' willingness to stock and support a new silicon vendor's module.

useCases.title: Commercial inspection and survey
useCases.buyer: Commercial drone manufacturers (airframe builders)
useCases.problem: Inspection and survey missions flown beyond visual line of sight, or in RF-congested environments, require onboard perception and navigation that does not depend on a continuous radio link to stay safe.
useCases.delivers: The kit supplies a flight-weight SoC2 compute module, camera and IMU sensing set, flight-controller interface and an SDK for airborne perception, enabling object detection, tracking and visual odometry entirely onboard.

useCases.title: Aerial perception compute (airframe OEM supply)
useCases.buyer: Airframe builders (direct channel)
useCases.problem: Drone OEMs need a qualified compute-and-perception subsystem they can integrate into their own airframes without designing custom silicon, while meeting weight and power budgets tighter than those of ground vehicles.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies the D100 as a drop-in kit, gimbal camera plus thermal sensor feeding SoC2 airborne perception, with telemetry relay to a ground station, so the airframe builder buys compute and builds the rest themselves.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The signal chain has four stages: cameras and an IMU read the scene and the airframe's own motion; SoC2 runs perception and visual odometry in flight; a planner produces waypoints or avoidance manoeuvres; and the flight controller executes them. The SoC2 stage is common to every SKU in the portfolio, the same perception compute running under different firmware. On the D100 specifically, fusing flight control, visual-inertial navigation and AI inference on one die eliminates the inter-chip bus, reducing latency, weight, power draw and failure points relative to a multi-chip architecture. The hardware fail-safe is the key differentiator: when the radio link or GPS fails, the flight-control loop reads VIO position directly on the same silicon and can fly the aircraft home without external input.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Demand is driven by onboard autonomy requirements in scenarios where a radio link cannot be relied upon, GPS jamming along contested borders and RF-congested urban or indoor environments are the primary triggers. The edge-AI drones segment is growing at an 18% CAGR (Mordor Intelligence), and India's defence establishment is already a paying customer: ₹1.01 Cr is contracted via MCEME / Indian Army with hardware fielded and reviewed by senior command. The D100 enters this market in FY2028 as ASIC-era silicon reaches production, the same year eight other SKUs begin earning revenue, so the ramp is gated by the same tapeout that funds the rest of the portfolio. Capture rates and pool-size assumptions are management projections; the underlying pool figures are third-party published estimates.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The primary dependency is drone regulation and form-factor development: regulatory clearance for autonomous or beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations directly gates commercial volume. The hardware constraint is weight and power budget, which is tighter in the air than on any ground vehicle, meaning the SoC2 module must meet airframe integration requirements that have no automotive equivalent. The defence channel requires sovereign procurement approval and continued Army engagement beyond the existing MCEME contract. Finally, because the D100 is the smallest and lightest configuration of the shared die, any silicon delay or yield issue affects all fifteen SKUs simultaneously, not just this one.

FY2032 revenue: ₹20.0 Cr at 400 units and 68% gross margin, equal to 1.8% of group revenue, management projection.

Demand pool growth rate: Edge-AI drones segment growing at 18% CAGR per Mordor Intelligence; FY2032 volume of 400 units is a single-digit share of the India defence and commercial drone SoC pool, capture rates are management assumptions.

thermal.lead: The Thermal Camera Pod is a bolt-on long-wave infrared sensor module that feeds DeepGrid's SoC2 compute box, extending detection capability through night, glare, dust, smoke and monsoon conditions where visible cameras degrade. At ₹50,000 per unit, it is positioned as a capability line rather than a profit line, its strategic role is to close the single largest gap in the camera-only perception stack.

useCases.title: Fleet night and monsoon upgrade
useCases.buyer: Fleets upgrading existing vehicles
useCases.problem: Commercial fleets operating at night and through the monsoon face sharply degraded camera-only detection, creating safety exposure that visible-light sensors cannot resolve.
useCases.delivers: A bolt-on LWIR pod with weatherised housing and lens heater that reads emitted heat rather than reflected light, feeding thermal detections into the same SoC2 object list as the visible cameras so the fleet's existing compute box gains all-condition perception without replacement.

useCases.title: Smart Truck kit attach sale
useCases.buyer: Fleets and integrators fitting the AD2 Smart Truck kit
useCases.problem: The Smart Truck's eleven-sensor suite requires a thermal channel on each mirror tower to ensure no quarter of the vehicle goes unobserved in low-visibility conditions; cameras and radar alone cannot supply heat-based separation of people and animals from roadside clutter at night.
useCases.delivers: One thermal camera per mirror tower, fused by SoC2 alongside the road-facing and 120-degree side cameras, so the truck kit retains detection capability in the conditions, glare, unlit road, dust, smoke, where the other channels degrade.

useCases.title: Aftermarket attach alongside AD0
useCases.buyer: Fleets and integrators fitting the AD0 Smart Mirror
useCases.problem: Operators who have already fitted a camera-based surround-view or ADAS module need a path to extend that investment to night and monsoon operation without replacing the base unit.
useCases.delivers: The thermal pod is sold through the same aftermarket fitment channel as the base kit, making it a second sale into an existing customer; the SoC2 compute box already present in the AD0 system accepts the thermal feed without additional compute hardware.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The LWIR sensor reads emitted heat rather than reflected light, so a person or animal appears bright against a cold road surface even in complete darkness or heavy smoke. SoC2 runs detection on the thermal image in parallel with the visible camera stream, classifying people and animals and separating them from roadside clutter. Detections join the same object list the visible cameras feed, so downstream safety outputs treat thermal and visible tracks uniformly. The lens heater in the weatherised housing keeps the optic clear through monsoon rain, which is precisely the condition that most degrades visible-light sensors.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: India's road-death profile, where two-wheeler riders and pedestrians together account for the majority of fatalities, is driving regulatory and fleet-safety pressure that makes all-condition perception commercially urgent rather than optional. Night and monsoon operation represent the single largest gap in camera-only ADAS fitments already being deployed under the ADAS mandate on N2/N3 vehicles, creating an immediate attach opportunity at the same fitment event. The thermal pod's first revenue is projected for FY2027, aligned with the Smart Truck kit and AD0 launches, so the channel and installation infrastructure are shared rather than built separately. The global automotive thermal camera market is estimated at $1.68 billion in 2025 with a 12% CAGR (Verified Market Research); DeepGrid's FY2032 volume of 3,200 units represents a 0.10% capture rate, which management treats as a conservative attach assumption against its own installed base.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The single most critical dependency is LWIR sensor supply: the thermal sensor is imported and is described as the highest bill-of-materials risk in the entire sensor group, meaning a supply disruption or price increase directly compresses margin or halts shipments with no domestic alternative identified. The calibration pipeline must scale alongside volume, since each pod requires individual calibration to integrate correctly with the SoC2 fusion stack. Revenue depends on the Smart Truck and AD0 programmes achieving their own FY2027 launch timelines, because the thermal pod has no standalone demand channel of comparable size. All revenue and volume figures are management projections; the capture rate of 0.10% against the global pool is a management assumption, not a contracted order.

h100.lead: The H100 Driver Monitor is a wrist-worn band that reads pulse and movement to detect driver drowsiness, feeding an alert chain without placing a camera in the cabin. At ₹5,000 and 50% gross margin, it is positioned as a fleet entry point, a channel line rather than a profit line, whose volume depends entirely on mandate enforcement timing.

useCases.title: Fleet drowsiness compliance (wearable route)
useCases.buyer: Fleets meeting drowsiness obligations without fitting a cabin camera
useCases.problem: Commercial fleets must satisfy AIS-184 (DDAWS) driver-drowsiness obligations but some operators prefer not to install an in-cab camera pointed at the driver's face, making driver acceptance a genuine adoption barrier.
useCases.delivers: A wrist-worn band that scores alertness on-device using pulse and motion data, then triggers the vehicle alert chain and notifies the fleet, satisfying the drowsiness obligation without cabin video.

useCases.title: OEM homologation for DDAWS standard
useCases.buyer: OEM homologation engineer and testing-agency assessor
useCases.problem: AIS-184 approval requires a ten-participant day-and-night study generating ten or more true-positive or false-negative events with per-participant sensitivity reported, a documentation burden, not merely a technical demonstration.
useCases.delivers: An in-cab drowsiness pipeline delivered together with the completed study package, including metrics, thresholds, activation speed, weather limits and statistical analysis, so the integrator receives an approvable documentation set.

useCases.title: Fleet-health SaaS upsell
useCases.buyer: Fleet safety manager
useCases.problem: Fleets operating large commercial vehicle pools need continuous driver-health monitoring and compliance logging across their entire operation, not just point-of-sale hardware.
useCases.delivers: The H100 wearable acts as the entry purchase in a fleet relationship, with fleet-health SaaS at ₹8L/truck/yr layered on top of the hardware, converting a ₹5,000 unit sale into recurring revenue.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The band reads pulse and movement continuously on the driver's wrist; an on-device model scores alertness without transmitting raw biometric data. When a drowsiness state crosses a threshold, the vehicle alert chain warns the driver and the fleet is notified. The H100 chiplet on the shared SoC2 die handles this computation, described as a custom bio-ADC fatigue processor and cabin monitoring interface, running the same perception compute as every other SKU under different firmware. The signal chain therefore runs entirely on hardware already present in the vehicle, with no separate compute module required.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: AIS-184 (DDAWS) under the ADAS mandate requires driver drowsiness and attention warning systems on new commercial vehicle models from 1 October 2027 and on all models from 1 January 2028. The buying decision for fleets and OEMs is when to comply, not whether to comply, because the standard does not permit non-fitment. The H100 wearable offers a lower-intrusion path to that same obligation for fleets where driver acceptance of in-cab cameras is a practical obstacle. DeepGrid's first revenue on this line is projected for FY2027, timed to the homologation window ahead of the mandate dates.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The product dossier identifies mandate enforcement timeline as the key dependency: if regulators delay or under-enforce AIS-184, the demand trigger that makes the buying decision compulsory weakens. The portfolio deck adds driver acceptance and enrolment discipline as an operational, not technical, risk: fleets must actually get drivers to wear and charge the band consistently, or the alert chain produces no useful signal. The narration notes that a wristband clears the acceptance hurdle more easily than an in-cab camera, but that advantage only holds if enrolment is maintained at scale. Capture rates in the demand pool are management assumptions, and pool sizes are third-party published estimates.

radar.lead: The 4D Radar Pod is a sealed, weatherproof imaging radar module delivering range, velocity, azimuth and elevation data that camera-only systems cannot measure. Its economic rationale rests on a single fact: the radar processing block already exists on the shared SoC2 die, so the tapeout cost is already paid.

useCases.title: Fleet and integrator radar upgrade
useCases.buyer: Fleets and integrators adding radar to camera-only fitments
useCases.problem: Camera-only ADAS systems degrade in rain, dust and glare, and cannot directly measure closing speed, the quantity a braking decision actually turns on. Fleets and integrators need a sensor that keeps working in the conditions where cameras fail.
useCases.delivers: A sealed aftermarket radar pod, mountable forward or on a corner, that feeds range, velocity and angle tracks into the existing compute box and fuses with the camera object list to confirm or reject detections.

useCases.title: Defensible braking evidence
useCases.buyer: Fleet operators and system integrators requiring auditable collision data
useCases.problem: Where a braking decision must be defensible after an incident, an estimated closing speed from a camera does not stand up; a directly measured figure from radar does.
useCases.delivers: The R100 radar DSP block on the SoC2 die converts raw returns into measured closing speed across frames, including through adverse conditions, providing a recorded, measured value rather than a camera estimate.

useCases.title: Smart Truck surround-sensor layer
useCases.buyer: OEM and Tier-1 integrators building full-surround AD2 truck kits
useCases.problem: A complete commercial-vehicle ADAS kit requires front and rear radar alongside cameras to achieve full surround coverage with animal and cyclist detection in adverse conditions.
useCases.delivers: Front and rear 77 GHz radar pods whose output the SoC2 fuses with seven RGB and two thermal cameras in 8.6 ms of the 33.3 ms frame, supplying the radar channel inside the Smart Truck AD2 kit.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The pod illuminates the forward or corner scene and reads the radar returns; the R100 block on the SoC2 die converts those returns into range, velocity and elevation. Tracks are formed and held across frames, remaining stable through rain, dust and glare, conditions where cameras degrade. Those tracks then fuse with the camera object list inside the SoC2 compute box to confirm or reject detections. Closing speed, the quantity a collision decision actually turns on, is measured by the radar rather than estimated, which is the functional distinction from a camera-only suite.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The global 4D imaging radar market is estimated at $2.75 billion in 2025 with a 13% CAGR, creating a growing pool of integrators seeking radar modules. Camera-only ADAS fitments are already in the field and operators are adding radar as a second layer rather than replacing full systems, which suits an aftermarket pod format. The ADAS mandate applying to N2/N3 commercial vehicles is accelerating sensor fitment across Indian fleets, raising demand for components that can be retrofitted. DeepGrid's pod is positioned to enter this market in FY2027, when the mandate retrofit cycle is expected to be active.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The pod is priced at ₹25,000 and carries a 50% gross margin, meaning the radar front-end and housing cost is recovered at half the selling price. The economic logic is explicit in the portfolio: the radar processing block is already on the shared SoC2 die and the tapeout has already been paid for across fifteen products, so incremental unit economics are not burdened by silicon development cost. Management projects 3,000 units shipped in FY2032, producing ₹7.5 Cr of revenue, 0.7% of the group plan. The line is described as the smallest in the plan and is not expected to carry the portfolio; its role is to monetise silicon capability that exists regardless.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The product depends on radar front-end supply and antenna qualification; the DSP processing is already on the die and is not a gating item. Radar block verification on the ASIC must complete before the pod can ship, making that milestone the primary technical gate for first revenue in FY2027. On the demand side, the FY2032 volume of 3,000 units represents a management-assumed 0.03% capture of the global 4D imaging radar pool, so the risk is not market size but the ability to win design-ins against established radar suppliers. Capital allocation guidance from the investment documents explicitly excludes funding a radar programme of any kind beyond what the existing die already provides, so the pod must be commercialised within the current silicon perimeter.

Road Autonomy.lead: Road Autonomy is DeepGrid Semi's largest product line, comprising three commercial-vehicle and indoor-vehicle ADAS kits, Smart Truck (AD2 Kit), AD0 Smart Mirror, and AD1 Indoor L4 Kit, sold primarily to fleet operators and commercial-vehicle buyers seeking driver-assistance and autonomy retrofits. The line is forecast to reach ₹762 Cr in FY2032, representing 67.5% of total plan revenue (management projection). It anchors the group's revenue plan, with first revenue expected in FY2027 across two of the three SKUs.

Silicon & Compute.lead: Silicon & Compute is DeepGrid Semi's semiconductor and compute-module product line, supplying bare SoC2 die to OEM board designers and a tiered range of PCIe and M.2 compute modules to systems integrators and industrial customers who embed AI perception into their own products. The line spans five members, from the Chipset OEM B2B die at ₹18,000 to the A100 Compute Box 4ch PCIe at ₹3,00,000, with first revenues projected by management to begin in FY2028 and FY2029. Under management projections, the line is forecast to reach ₹194.3 Cr in FY2032, representing 17.2% of plan revenue.

Fleet & Mobility.lead: Fleet & Mobility is DeepGrid Semi's two-SKU autonomous-vehicle operations line, comprising Autonomous TaaS (contracted route operations at ₹66.00 L per vehicle, first revenue FY2028) and Seaport AGV (container-yard automation at ₹45,30,000 per unit, first revenue FY2028); its buyers are fleet operators benchmarking cost per tonne-kilometre against driven alternatives and port terminal operators seeking yard automation; as a management projection, the line is forecast to reach ₹88.6 Cr in FY2032, representing 7.9% of plan revenue, with both members targeting 89% gross margin.

Sensors & Robotics.lead: Sensors & Robotics is DeepGrid Semi's hardware perception line, spanning defence robotics, aerial compute kits, and automotive sensing components sold to defence procurement agencies, drone airframe builders, and commercial vehicle fleets. The line targets buyers who require silicon-level perception capability, from in-cabin driver monitoring to 4D radar and long-wave infrared imaging, across both regulated safety mandates and defence programmes. Management projects the line will reach ₹83.5 Cr in FY2032, representing 7.4% of plan revenue.
